scientific_queries.note: Bridges C24 (weak unseen-drug prediction) with C27 (decision value) on GDSC.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round tests a never-asked bridge question and flags the confound in its own secondary comparison.

design.holdout: 20% of the 65 drugs held out; training uses only keys whose two drugs are both seen

headline: a prediction with R2 = 0.029 still lifts top-20 hits from 1.38% to 4.88% on drugs never seen in training - a 3.5x gain
significance: this separates 'is the prediction accurate' from 'is it useful for decisions': near-zero variance explained coexists with a large decision gain
confound_disclosed: the seen_only control is much weaker here (+0.37 pp at k=20) than C27's 6.50% because training excludes every key containing a held-out drug; H166 must therefore not be read as 'unseen is better than seen'
limits: drug-level holdout with cells still overlapping: this is unseen-drug, not unseen-cell
the both-unseen subset is marginal (CI lower bound exactly 0.0000)
pool sizes vary with the number of held-out drugs
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI

register_updates.C41: new, exploratory: the weak unseen-drug signal has decision value

next_gates: test whether the gain survives when the pool shrinks to a few hundred candidates
